title: Two-storey column with beams: second-order moments under vertical and lateral load

source.work: McGuire, W., Gallagher, R. H., Ziemian, R. D., Matrix Structural Analysis
source.location: Example 9.5, case 2 (alpha = 0.01, P = 3978 kN), moment diagram for Eq. 8.3
source.notes: input data and targets read on the cited pages; nothing of the source is reproduced

analysis: Plane (x-y) problem of the source modelled in 3D with the global Y axis vertical, so that the source's x, y and theta_z are the model's X, Y and rz. In-plane bending is about local z for every member (default orientation), hence the source's I is the section's Iz. a (0, 0), b (0, 6), c (0, 10), d (4, 6), e (4, 10) m. Column ab-bc: A = 2.5e4 mm^2, I = 6.36e8 mm^4; beams bd, ce (rigidly connected to the column): A = 1.76e4 mm^2, I = 8.61e8 mm^4; E = 200,000 MPa. a is pinned; d and e are on rollers that hold the vertical displacement only (as drawn in the source). Loads: P = 3978 kN (0.6 of the source's critical load) downward at c, 0.01 P along +x at c and at b. Second-order analysis. Targets: the second-order values of the source's moment diagram (figure labels, kN m): 932 in the column below b, 869 in beam bd at b, 272 at joint c. The engine's members carry the exact stability functions (no discretisation error for a prismatic member with constant axial force); the source's computed values use a stated number of elements with a polynomial (approximate) geometric stiffness. The source models each member as a single element and states that column bowing is not included in the displayed results. Plane stability problem: the source's model has no out-of-plane degrees of freedom. Here the out-of-plane DOFs (uz, rx, ry) of every node are held and Iy = 1000 Iz, so that no out-of-plane buckling mode precedes the in-plane modes compared; J is a placeholder.

quarantine.diagnosis: All three targets missed by 3 % to 4.5 %: engine -971.71, 908.02, 280.31 kN m; figure labels of the source 932, 869, 272 kN m. The source's values come from an incremental analysis with one element per member whose solution scheme and step size are not stated; no error bound is given. Evidence that the difference is not the source's discretisation: the source's own element matrices (Eq. 4.34 with the geometric stiffness of Eq. 9.14, one element per member), solved here to equilibrium with the member axial forces iterated, give 971.5, 907.8 and 280.3 kN m - the engine's values within 0.03 % - so the difference of 4 % lies in the source's solution process (an incremental scheme without equilibrium iteration underestimates the displacements of a softening structure; the source discusses this drift in its Section 12.2) or in its geometry updating, which cannot be determined from the example. Separately, tier C does not pass on this model: PyNite is not eligible (estimated approximation error 4.1e-2 above the limit 5e-3) and the difference to OpenSeesPy, 5.85e-4 (rotation at a), exceeds the allowed 5.84e-4 (1e-6 plus the estimated OpenSees discretisation error, which is not a bound). Read off a figure; approximate method in the source.
